title: First Project
text:
The goal of this project is for you to demonstrate proficiency in the material we have covered in this class (and beyond, if you like) and apply them to a ‘novel’ data set of your choosing in a meaningful way. You are not asked to do an exhaustive data analysis by generating every statistic/visualizations that we have learned of in the course. Rather, I expect you to demonstrate skills in asking meaningful questions and answering them using carefully selected data analysis techniques and tools. These analyses must be done in R in a reproducible manner (quarto).
Several data sets are available but your group will choose just one to use for this project. After choosing the data set, your will need to brainstorm on several issues about the data such as the sample and sampling methods that might have been used to gather the data, a possible target population, variables and their types (numerical vs categorical), among others. Your team will then come up with a research topic/goal and two research questions (directly related to the topic) that you will answer by conducting the analyses. Your analyses should include both numerical summary statistics and visualizations. The visualizations (and statistics) generated must be appropriately linked to help tell a coherent story.

title: First Project
text:
Abstract
The abstract should be a brief summary of your research topic, questions, data, methods, and findings. It should be no more than 250 words. It is best to write the abstract after you are done with all the other parts of the project.

title: First Project
text:
Introduction
The introduction section introduces your topic and provides the background. In this section, you will need to provide a rationale for your chosen topic and/.or questions and describe why we should care. Possible benefits of your study should be included. Consider citing a few articles in the introduction section to help you make your case.

title: First Project
text:
Research Questions
Write down two research questions that you will answer as part of your study. Both questions should address your research topic. In other words, you should not have questions that are unrelated as this might suggest you are doing two different studies in one. The variables of interest should be clearly identified in each question.
Note that you are not required to answer both questions in the same way. For example, you can use descriptive statistics and visualizations (exploratory) to answer one question and simple linear regression (predictive) tools to answer the other.

title: First Project
text:
Literature Review
Find 5 to 7 articles about your topic, read and synthesize them to show what previous researchers have done on that topic. If the articles were empirical studies, you need to state the rationale for the study, the methods used (e.g. experimental, observational), findings, etc. The goal is to situate your own study in the context of existing studies/literature.

title: First Project
text:
Methods
The methods section should describe the data and the methods used to analyze the data. This section should include the following subsections:

Sample and Sampling Method
Describe your sample and its characteristics. How large is the sample and how was it collected (e.g., what instruments were used)? What is the target population? What sampling method was used and how does this impact whether or not the sample is representative of the population?  Note that since you are using existing data that you did not collect, I will allow you to speculate on some of the data collection techniques as long as the speculation seems reasonable. You will do this only when you cannot fine enough information in the documentation for the data set of your choice.


Data Analysis Techniques
Describe the data analysis techniques that are used to answer each of your research questions. This section should include a description of the variables used in the analysis, their types (numerical vs categorical), and how they were measured. You should also describe any data wrangling (cleaning) or transformation that was done before the analysis. Finally, you should describe the statistical methods used to analyze the data (e.g., summary statistics, visualizations, regression models, etc.) and why they are appropriate for your research questions.

title: First Project
text:
Data Analysis and Results
This section includes the actual analyses discussed under methodology section above. Each analysis tool should be accompanied by an interpretation and discussion in light of the research questions. Numerical summary statistics and visualizations, however nice they may be, do not have much meaning on their own. You as the author of the report must give them meaning through the interpretations that you make. The analysis and interpretations of outputs should be organized by research question.

title: First Project
text:
Conclusion
Finally, you will need to write a conclusion of your report. In the conclusion, you want to briefly restate what you set out to do and how you went about it. Give some brief summary on the data used, data explorations/analyses performed and the results obtained. What insights did you draw from your analyses? Do your findings agree with existing literature? Are there any surprises? Discuss the potential implications of your work (i.e., what practical consequences does your study have?) Lastly, reflect on possible limitations of your study and how future similar studies might be better designed.

title: First Project
text:
References
All sources used should be cited both in text and listed under references. Use the APA format. You may find the APA referencing guide on this link.

title: Final Project
text: The goal of this project is to apply what you have learned in this course to conduct exploratory and inferential statistical analysis. Multiple data frames are available but your group will choose only one to use for the project. You will need to browse the available data sets, their variables, etc, and come up with possible research questions that can be answered using the data. Your group will narrow down to two or three interesting research questions then use the various tools learned in the course to explore patterns in the data (exploratory analysis) then use statistical inference tools (hypotheses tests and confidence intervals) taught in the course to run inferential analysis. Your exploratory analysis should include both numerical statistics (e.g., means, medians, proportions, etc.) and visualizations (e.g., histograms, bar plots, box plots, etc.). Your inferential analysis should use both hypotheses tests and confidence intervals.

title: Final Project
text:
Abstract
The abstract is a brief summary of your research topic, questions, data, methods, key findings, and implications of the findings. It should be no more than 250 words.

title: Final Project
text:
Introduction
This section introduces your topic and provides background information. You should explain the rationale for your study and why it is important to investigate. Be sure to include the potential benefits of your research. In addition, cite a few relevant previous studies to support your argument. Refer to the project example for guidance on how to structure your introduction.

title: Final Project
text:
Research Questions & Hypotheses
Write down two research questions that you will answer in your study. Both questions should clearly relate to your research topic. Avoid including unrelated questions, as this may indicate that you are conducting two separate studies within one project. The variables of interest should be clearly identified in each question.
Since your questions will be addressed using statistical inference, you should also include the corresponding hypotheses for each question.

title: Final Project
text:
Literature Review
Find 5 to 7 articles related to your topic, read them, and synthesize their findings to summarize what previous researchers have reported. The goal is to place your study within the context of existing literature. This section should be approximately five paragraphs in length.

title: Final Project
text:
Methodology
The methods section should describe the data and the methods used to analyze the data. This section should include the following subsections:

Sample and Data Collection Methods
Describe your sample, the cases, and their characteristics (e.g., if you the cases are people, what’s their age? gender?, etc). How large is the sample and how was it collected (e.g., what instruments were used?). What is the target population? What sampling method was used and how does this impact whether or not the sample is representative of the population?  Note that since you are using existing data that you did not collect, you are allowed to speculate on some of the data collection techniques as long as the speculation seems reasonable. You will do this only when you cannot find enough information in the documentation for the data set of your choice.


Description of Data Analysis Techniques
Briefly describe the data analysis techniques you will use to answer each of your research questions and justify your choices. This section should include a description of the variables used in the analysis, including their types (numerical or categorical) and how they were measured.
You should also explain any data cleaning or transformations performed prior to the analysis. If you created a categorical variable from a numerical variable, describe this step and provide a rationale for doing so.
Finally, outline the statistical methods you will use to analyze the data. Your description should include both exploratory and inferential analyses. Exploratory analysis should include summary statistics and data visualizations. Inferential statistics should involve hypothesis testing and confidence intervals. This section may or may not include visualizations, depending on your analysis. You must also provide a justification for your choice of analysis methods (e.g., inference for two independent means is appropriate because the question involves….).

title: Final Project
text:
Data Analysis, Results, and Discussion
In this section, you will carry out the analyses described above and report your findings. All outputs (such as graphs, summary statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals) must be accompanied by interpretations in the context of your study and should directly address the original research questions.
Organize the section by research question. For each question, include both exploratory and inferential analyses.

Conclusion

State the insights drawn from the study and compare to existing findings reported under literature review section. Discuss the potential implications of your work (i.e., what practical consequences does your study have?) Lastly, reflect on limitations of your study and how future similar studies might be better designed.
